subject: Pilot: early cancellation mitigation request - Stella Health
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@stellahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot: early cancellation mitigation request - Stella Health

Jordan —

Thanks for the call this morning. Per Stella’s procurement team, they want explicit 'early opt-out' language for the 90-day pilot that allows them to terminate with 30 days notice without full commitment. They’re asking that we remove the standard ramp schedule penalties for pilots.

We’ve proposed an alternate addendum that preserves most protections for Redwood while giving Stella the flexibility to walk if the integration shows low signal. The ask is: can Deal Desk / Execs approve the attached addendum that replaces the 90-day ramp penalty with a scaled mitigation fee and a reduced notice window?

Key points in our draft (attached):
- Pilot term: 90 days; customer may opt-out with 30 days written notice.
- Mitigation fee: 25% of remaining committed spend for next two months (capped at $15k) if they opt out in first 90 days.
- Downsell protection: if they remain but reduce committed capacity, Redwood reserves right to tier pricing for reduced throughput for 60 days before recalculation.
- Requirement: production data/usage summary to validate signal before refund/proration.

Attachments: Stella_Pilot_Addendum_v1.docx (redline) and Redwood-Terms-Addendum_v2.pdf

We need an executive decision around the mitigation fee cap and whether finance should reserve holdback in the contract immediately. Jordan, copied procurement, is willing to sign if we can limit the worst-case exposure.

Can Karthik and Neha weigh in on cost exposure and legal acceptability? If we get a quick green light I’ll send back an updated addendum and DocuSign link.

—Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot: early cancellation mitigation request - Stella Health

FW: copying leadership for a quick decision.

Quick summary:
- Customer: Stella Health — high potential (PoC -> production likely if signal positive).
- Ask: Remove/exempt 90-day ramp penalty; instead accept opt-out w/ mitigation fee and cap.
- Financial exposure (approx): If they cancel immediately, using proposed cap we lose at most ~$15k; without cap we could be looking at ~60k over 2 months at their committed run rate.

Recommendation (deal desk position): Approve the opt-out language subject to:
1) Mitigation fee set at 25% of remaining committed spend for the next 2 months, capped at $15k.
2) Limit this exception to pilot deals <= $50k ARR and to first-time pilots (one per account per region).
3) Finance to place a temporary hold/reserve against the deal in our booking system until DocuSign completes.
4) Legal to approve final redline to ensure the language doesn't create a broad termination precedent.

If Legal (Neha) is comfortable with the wording, I support moving forward — it materially reduces friction for Stella and keeps worst-case exposure within an acceptable band for the sales motion.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot: early cancellation mitigation request - Stella Health

Thanks — reviewed. A few legal items to tighten before we present an exec-approved addendum: 

1) Opt-out notice: change to 'written notice of intent to terminate no less than 30 calendar days' and require completion of a brief exit checklist to support our mitigation calculation (data export, last 2 weeks usage, point of contact).
2) Mitigation fee: 25% of remaining committed spend for the next two billing cycles is fine, but reduce cap to $12,500 and add a clause that the fee is waived if customer demonstrates <10% production signal (to avoid penalizing technically unsuccessful integrations).
3) Downsell protection: define 'reduced capacity' clearly by reference to the committed token throughput or seat count; require 60-day stabilization window before price tier changes.
4) Precedent clause: add 'This addendum applies solely to the pilot referenced in Deal RDW-2026-1043 and is not a company-wide amendment.'

I’ve attached a redline (redline_optout_clause.docx). Once we have internal sign-off I can approve the final language for DocuSign.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot: early cancellation mitigation request - Stella Health

Thanks team — I approve the exception with the following executive conditions:

1) Cap the mitigation fee at $12,500 (per Legal's redline) and include the waiver if <10% production signal.
2) Limit the exception to pilots <= $50k ARR and mark the Deal Desk record as 'pilot-early-cancel-exception' for audit.
3) Finance must place a $12,500 reserve in the booking ledger until the DocuSign completes; treasury to release pro-rata after 30 days of continued usage.
4) Sales to attach the signed addendum and the usage snapshot to the HubSpot deal (link copied below).

Jordan — please confirm you’re comfortable with the capped mitigation and the exit checklist. If yes, Rachel can push DocuSign and we’ll route the booking hold to Finance.
